Blinking rate increases with stress, anxiety, or cognitive load — also with attraction

Gaze aversion (looking away) can indicate discomfort, lying, or simply thinking — context is essential

Looking down signals submission, shame, or sadness — but also can signal respect in some cultures
Rapid eye movements (searching) can indicate anxiety or active information processing
Lateral gaze (looking left or right) has been controversially linked to lying — use with caution, no solid evidence
Staring without blinking is a primate threat display — seen in confrontations

Ear pulling, rubbing, or tugging signals stress, indecision, or discomfort with what is being discussed

People who touch their nose when answering a question may be experiencing stress, but NOT necessarily lying
Nose touching increases during cold weather and allergy season — always consider environmental factors
Nose pinch (pinching the bridge of the nose with eyes closed) signals fatigue, frustration, or overwhelming stress
Subtle nose flare may be the only sign of suppressed anger before an outburst
